main_body: A church pew seen from the side (east/west profile): a tall brown backrest plank on the left and a seat section on the right with three red cushion panels separated by wooden bands.
top_band: Only a thin 2-row light-brown strip (rows ~14-15) at the top of the seat area; the backrest top is a 1-2px dark cap. No real top surface is visible.
evidence: The pew is drawn as a flat vertical profile or elevation. The left column is a tall backrest plank seen edge-on. The right side is a stack of three red cushion panels, each a vertical face, with only a 2px light strip at the top. Seat surfaces are not shown from above as horizontal bands. The red blocks are stacked face-on with thin brown dividers (1-2 rows) and no foreshortened seat tops. This matches the 'side elevation' failure in the guide, a profile with no horizontal surface visible from above.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tone that matches the wood, which is good. However, the red cushions are large flat fills of one red with only a darker edge, and the wood planks are nearly flat with 2-3 tones and no grain. Beodeul references (the stall and the well) carry per-tile highlights, grain, and many tones. The candidate has far fewer colours per tile and is flatter and thinner than the references.
